title: The HPE engine moved the drive-belt interval from 15,000 km to 10,000 km — the older schedule leaves an HPE belt 5,000 km late
description: Two Vespa schedules exist for the same 300 cm3 class and they disagree. The GTS 300 i.e. ABS owner's manual (Ed. 04_04/2018, Cod. 1Q000478; the same page also carries 1Q000479 for the other language set) schedules the drive belt for replacement at 15,000, 30,000, 45,000 and 60,000 km, valve clearance adjustment at 20,000, 40,000 and 60,000 km, and the spark plug every 10,000 km. The GTS 300 HPE ABS service station manual (1Q000725) and the GTS 310 HPE owner's manual (Ed. 02-05_2025, Cod. 1Q001103, USA edition) schedule the belt every 10,000 km, valve clearance every 10,000 km, and the plug every 20,000 km. The HPE manual says why: 'AFTER THE SCHEDULED MAINTENANCE PROGRAM IS FINISHED YOU ARE TOLD TO PROCEED WITH THE MAINTENANCE OF THE VEHICLE STARTING FROM THE SERVICE COUPON OF 10,000 km (6,214 miles) OR 10 MONTHS' — the engine moved to a 10,000 km service cycle and the belt moved with it. Mileage figures exist only in the HPE service manual's separate 'FOR USA-LATAM VERSION' table and in the USA owner's manual; the EU owner's manuals are kilometres only. All four documents were read from mirror copies: Piaggio serves vespa.com and manuals.vespa.com with HTTP 403 to every non-browser client. Intervals here were read by column position in the maintenance grid, not by counting marks, because plain text extraction destroys the column alignment.
model: GTS 300, GTS 300 HPE, GTV 300, GTS 310 HPE, GTS Super 300
symptoms: when to change the vespa belt
causes: Applying the pre-HPE 15,000 km schedule to an HPE engine
Using an EU manual, which prints no mileage columns, on a US machine
fix_procedure: 1. Establish whether the machine is HPE before quoting an interval: the schedule differs by engine, not by displacement. 2. On an HPE, use 10,000 km (6,200 mi) for the drive belt and the valve clearance, and 20,000 km for the plug. 3. On a pre-HPE GTS 300 i.e., use 15,000 km for the belt, 20,000 km for the valves and 10,000 km for the plug. 4. Read intervals from the column the mark sits under. 5. The US mileage columns exist only in the HPE service manual and the USA owner's manual.

title: Vespa and Piaggio manuals are VIN-gated or dealer-only — what a technician can actually obtain, and what is published openly
description: Piaggio does not publish owner's manuals as open downloads. manuals.vespa.com and manuals.piaggio.com take a first name, surname, email, country, post code and the frame number, and deliver the booklet by email: 'The frame/chassis number is needed to allow us to provide you with the correct use and maintenance booklet for your model', and 'This service is available for vehicles produced from 2004.' Both hosts, and vespa.com itself, return an Akamai HTTP 403 to every non-browser client — curl with or without a browser user-agent, and automated fetchers alike — so an automated link check will report them dead when they are merely gated. Service station manuals are a separate class and say so: 'This service station manual has been drawn up by Piaggio & C. Spa to be used by the workshops of Piaggio-Gilera dealers.' What Piaggio does publish openly are one-page maintenance-interval sheets on its own asset host for a few ranges — Medley 125-150, Liberty 125-150, Liberty 50, Beverly 350, a US Typhoon sheet, and an MP3 500 hpe sheet. Those sheets are summaries and omit items the full manuals schedule: the MP3 500 hpe sheet lists oil, filters, belt, plugs, coolant and brake fluid, and does not mention the roll-lock cable adjustment that the full manual schedules at every interval. The Piaggio Group dealer tooling is already described in this knowledge base under Aprilia and Moto Guzzi; this entry does not restate it.
symptoms: where to get a vespa manual
causes: Expecting an open PDF library where Piaggio operates a VIN-gated request form
Treating an Akamai 403 as a dead document rather than a gated one
fix_procedure: 1. For an owner's manual, use the manuals request form with the frame number; it covers machines built from 2004 onward. 2. Expect a 403 from any scripted fetch of vespa.com, manuals.vespa.com or manuals.piaggio.com; that is the gate, not a broken link. 3. For workshop data, the service station manual is a dealer document. 4. Piaggio's own public interval sheets are summaries: check the full manual before telling an owner an item is not scheduled.

title: Piaggio calls it the OBD port, but it is a six-pin Piaggio connector — a generic 16-pin scan tool does not plug into a Vespa
description: The Vespa GTS 300 HPE ABS service station manual (1Q000725) gives the connector Piaggio names the 'OBD port' as six pins: 1 key-on power supply input (Yellow/Black, from fuse F6), 2 CAN H line (Pink/Red), 3 ground (Black), 4 battery power supply input from its own 5 A protection fuse (Red/Yellow), 5 CAN L line (Pink/White), 6 K line (Orange/Black). That is not the 16-pin SAE J1962 layout, and no Piaggio document read for this entry uses the terms OBD-II, OBD2, J1962 or EOBD anywhere. The same manual names the engine control unit 'MIUG4' and maps its 32 pins across the HV coil, lambda probe, engine temperature sensor, pickup, injection loads and electric fan. The manual makes the dealer tool a condition of the service, not an option: 'AT EACH SCHEDULED MAINTENANCE MUST BE VERIFIED WITH THE DIAGNOSTIC TOOL IF THERE ARE ERRORS AND THE IF THE PARAMETERS ARE CORRECT' — the doubled wording is the document's own — and 'Diagnosis by tool' carries a mark in every column of every schedule, including the time columns. Ignition advance is tool-only: 'The ignition advance value is detectable at any time using the diagnostic tool.' No owner's manual read for this entry mentions the connector at all. The 2022 MP3 530 hpe owner's manual (Cod. 1Q000957) names 'an OBD (On-Board Diagnostics) port' and states no protocol, no pinout, no bus speed and no connector type in 184 pages. Read from mirror copies; Piaggio serves these documents 403 to non-browser clients.
model: GTS 300 HPE, GTS 310 HPE, MP3 530 hpe
symptoms: will a generic scan tool work on a vespa
causes: Reading the words 'OBD port' as a promise of a 16-pin J1962 socket
Expecting the owner's manual to locate the connector
fix_procedure: 1. Do not expect a generic 16-pin scan tool to mate with this connector: the manual documents six pins. 2. CAN H, CAN L and a K line are present; no Piaggio document read here states the protocol or bus speed. 3. The port is fed from battery through its own 5 A fuse as well as a key-on supply, so it can be live with the key off. 4. Expect the connector to appear only in the service station manual. 5. Ignition advance and calibration state are readable only through the dealer tool.

title: The MP3 roll lock engages only on four conditions at once, and the failure lamp means two different things — the audible alarm is what separates them
description: On the tilting three-wheeler the front suspension lock is conditional. The MP3 LT 400 i.e. owner's manual (Ed. 2, 2008) states engagement 'is possible only if the following conditions occur at the same time': throttle completely untwisted, engine below 2,500 rpm, vehicle speed below 10 km/h, and the failure lamp off. The MP3 530 hpe manual (Ed. 02_07/2022, Cod. 1Q000957) keeps both figures unchanged fourteen years later. Two lamps exist: one for the locking system and one for its failure. The failure lamp does not decode two ways but three, and the discriminator is sound, not cadence: flashing means a system failure; steady with no alarm means the rider is not properly seated, since 'THE RIDER DETECTION SENSOR IS LOCATED IN THE FRONT PART OF THE SADDLE. AVOID PLACING BAGS OR HEAVY OBJECTS ACCIDENTALLY ON THE SADDLE'; and steady with the continuous alarm is a stuck lock, which the manual answers with 'it can be unlocked by operating the «T» switch twice quickly on the unlocking position «2»', after which the machine is usable with the locking system disengaged. The 2022 manual drops the word 'steadily' from the not-seated case, so the mapping is per-edition. Release is by throttle, not by speed: 'the suspension locking system is disengaged automatically and the warning light turns off when the throttle is twisted to start the ride', with 2022 adding that the rider must be seated. A failure may cap the machine: 'For some cases of failure, the vehicle speed is auto-limited to 30 Km/h.' That sentence is character-identical in 2008 and 2022. The 2022 manual adds a warning the 2008 one does not have: with the engine on and the suspension still locked, as the rider takes the riding position, the injection system waits about half a second before answering the throttle. Read from mirror copies.
model: MP3 400, MP3 500, MP3 500 HPE, MP3 530 hpe
symptoms: mp3 locks when i sit down
causes: One of the four engagement conditions not met
A bag or heavy object on the front of the saddle reading as a rider
A locking-system failure, which may also cap road speed
fix_procedure: 1. Before treating a refusal to lock as a fault, check all four conditions: throttle closed, under 2,500 rpm, under 10 km/h, failure lamp off. 2. Read the failure lamp with the alarm, not alone: flashing is a system failure; steady without an alarm points at rider detection; steady with the continuous alarm is a stuck lock. 3. For a stuck lock, operate the lock switch twice quickly to the unlocking position; the machine then rides with the system disengaged. 4. Clear the front of the saddle before diagnosing a rider-detection complaint. 5. A 30 km/h cap is documented behaviour under some failures, not a separate fault. 6. Confirm the lamp wording against the edition in front of you.

title: Servicing the MP3 roll lock: a three-step reset, four test values, and a control unit the manuals call three different names
description: The MP3 400 i.e. service station manual (664502 IT, 664503 EN through 664509 EL, 2008) gives the tilting suspension its own control unit, separate from the engine control unit, sitting on the diagnostic line — the schematic lands the diagnostic line on the roll-lock unit at pin 2C while the engine unit connects at 2A and 2B, and the manual carries a labour code for replacing it. Resetting it after mechanical work is three steps, not one: SYSTEM RESET then LOWER STOP SEARCH; then PARAMETERS, where the geared-motor set screw is adjusted to a relative potentiometer angle of 12 degrees, with the note that 'a slight oscillation of the angle value between 0.00° and 0.50° is considered normal'; and then SYSTEM RESET again for POTENTIOMETER RESET. Of that last step the manual says 'If this is not successful, the tilt locking mechanism remains locked for safety' — a statement about that bench procedure, not about the machine's behaviour in service, where the owner's manual documents a failure leaving the lock disengaged with a 30 km/h cap. Four values are published for the circuit: the locking potentiometer reads 4 V activated and 1 V at rest, measured on pins 17 and 25 with the interface wiring connected, the machine on its centre stand, key on, meter on the 20 V scale; the rider-presence sensor reads about 3 kOhm seated and 15 to 18 kOhm not seated on pins 17 and 36; the caliper sensor is 'a normally opened switch'; the wheel-speed sensors read between 774 and 946 Ohm at about 20 degrees. The system is hydraulic and has its own pump. Two traps for anyone matching on strings: the fluid-level check appears in the pre-delivery chapter, not in the scheduled maintenance table, whose only roll-lock item is adjusting the caliper control cable at every interval; and one unit is called the tilt locking system control unit, the parking control unit and the parking electrical control unit in one manual, while the 2008 owner's manual calls one switch R in its legend, F in the body text and T throughout the chapter that describes using it. Read from mirror copies.
causes: A reset stopped after the lower stop search, omitting the potentiometer reset
Searching the manual on a component name or switch letter that the same manual uses inconsistently
fix_procedure: 1. Run the reset as three steps and finish with POTENTIOMETER RESET; stopping earlier leaves the job incomplete. 2. Set the relative potentiometer angle to 12 degrees; oscillation up to half a degree is documented as normal. 3. Test the potentiometer at 4 V locked and 1 V at rest on pins 17 and 25, with the interface wiring connected and the machine on its centre stand. 4. Test rider presence at about 3 kOhm seated against 15 to 18 kOhm unseated on pins 17 and 36. 5. Treat the caliper sensor as normally open. 6. Search this system by function, not by switch letter or unit name: both vary within a single manual. 7. The fluid-level check is a pre-delivery item; do not quote it as scheduled.

title: Four brake campaigns, one supplier and two different platings — the second plating was the fix for the first, and it failed too
description: Between November 2019 and April 2022 Piaggio filed four NHTSA campaigns for the same failure mode across two marques: hydrogen released from the plating of brake line or hose terminals into the brake fluid. The supplier named in the Part 573 reports is J.JUAN S.A of Spain. Three concern zinc plating. Campaign 19V826000 covers 2019 Vespa GTV 300 and GTS 300 and 2020 GTS 300 HPE, 1,328 units: 'The brake lines may have been improperly galvanized, allowing hydrogen to be released into the brake fluid', remedied by installing front and rear master-cylinder flush fittings and flushing the system. Campaign 20V524000 covers 2019-2020 Piaggio MP3 500, 123 units, for 'non-conformity of the zinc plating surface treatment of the brake hose terminals', and gives the field sign a technician will actually meet: 'Excessive play in the brake levers/pedal after the vehicle has been sitting for an extended period of time.' Campaign 22V217000 covers 2020-2021 MP3 500 HPE, 27 units, citing FMVSS 105 and 106. The fourth is not the same plating. Campaign 20V617000, 2020-2021 Vespa GTS 300 and GTV 300, concerns 'non-conformity of the zinc/nickel plating' on the zinc-nickel brake lines fitted on the assembly line from 5 May 2020 — that is, on the lines that replaced the earlier ones. Its remedy is conditional on the machine's age rather than uniform. Two of these reports disagree with themselves on how many machines are affected, and one campaign's Piaggio reference number appears only from the first amendment, not in the original filing.
model: GTS 300, GTV 300, GTS 300 HPE, MP3 500, MP3 500 HPE
causes: Hydrogen released from improperly plated brake line or hose terminals into the brake fluid
On the later campaign, the zinc-nickel plating that had replaced the earlier zinc process
fix_procedure: 1. Take excessive lever travel after a machine has stood for a while as the documented sign, not as ordinary air in the system. 2. Check the machine against all four campaigns: two marques and two plating processes are involved, and a machine built after May 2020 is not automatically outside the problem. 3. The remedies differ: a flush with added fittings on the earlier campaigns, and an age-conditional procedure on the 2020 one. 4. Confirm the current campaign text and the affected build dates against the campaign record before quoting a remedy.

title: A Vespa recall caused by servicing: reusing the exhaust gasket after a rear tyre change melted the rear brake hose
description: NHTSA campaign 07V253000, 2,757 machines, is the rare recall whose stated cause is a service practice rather than a part. The owner letter says: 'This leak is caused by the repeated removal and reinstallation of the muffler, for instance when replacing the rear tire, without the required replacement of the exhaust gasket.' The consequence is in the campaign record: 'THE REAR BRAKE HOSE MAY BE IMPAIRED OR MELTED, INCREASING THE RISK OF A CRASH.' The dealer bulletin adds that replacing the gasket 'is a service practice recommended by Vespa Piaggio, as stated in the Owners Manual', and the remedy replaced the header, pipe, clamp and gasket. Two details matter when searching. First, the word: NHTSA's summary calls the part a bushing, while Piaggio's own owner letter and dealer bulletin say gasket throughout and never use bushing — a technician searching the service literature will be using Piaggio's word. Second, the scope: the campaign record's model field reads only Vespa GTS for 2006 and 2007, and the restriction 'This situation affects the Vespa GTS 250 i.e. model only' appears in the owner letter, not in the record. The Part 573 report itself is a scanned image and cannot be read as text.
causes: Refitting the muffler without renewing the exhaust gasket, typically after a rear tyre change
Exhaust gas leaking past the reused gasket onto the rear brake hose
fix_procedure: 1. Renew the exhaust gasket every time the muffler comes off; the manual calls for it and the recall exists because it was reused. 2. Inspect the rear brake hose for heat damage on any machine with a history of muffler removal. 3. Search Piaggio literature for gasket and the regulator record for bushing; they describe the same part. 4. Confirm the machine against the campaign, whose record names the model family while the owner letter restricts it to the 250 i.e.

title: What the US regulator record covers for these machines — and the model years where no record can be retrieved at all
description: Ten NHTSA campaigns were retrieved for Piaggio Group scooters: 07V253000 (Vespa GTS exhaust gasket), 09V188000 (BV 500 and X9 500 fuel hose, 2,428 units), 11V603000 (ignition control unit altering timing so that 'IMPROPER IGNITION TIMING MAY CAUSE AN ENGINE BACKFIRE INTO THE AIRBOX', covering Fly 50 4T 4-valve 2011-2012, Vespa LX50 4T 2010-2012 and Vespa S50 4T 2009-2012, 2,147 units), 14V364000 (Vespa 946 fuel line, 305 units), 15V066000 (fuel pump, 2,613 units, whose machines 'may stall while being operated or may fail to restart after being shut off for 15-20 minutes', covering Vespa GTS, GTV and GTS Super 250 and 300, LX 150, LXV 150 and S 150, and Piaggio MP3 250, BV 250 Tourer and BV 300 Tourer), the four brake-plating campaigns, and 26V302000 (285 machines whose mirrors lack the convex warning, in one colourway only). What the record does not support is a claim of completeness. NHTSA's own model index flags model years as recall-affected for which no endpoint will return a campaign: 2006 and 2007 LX150, 2012 GTS 250, 2013, 2015 GTS 300, 2018 GTS RST and 2021 Primavera 150. The 2006-2007 LX150 window is unverified, not recall-free: 07V253000 restricts itself to the GTS 250 and 15V066000 starts at 2011 for the LX 150. Treat this record as near-complete for the GTS and GTV line and from 2019 onward, and as incomplete elsewhere. Two further cautions for anyone querying that data: the manufacturer name is recorded three different ways across the filings, but Piaggio's own signed reports use one form throughout, so the variation is data entry rather than a change of company; and the make field itself moves between Piaggio and Vespa for the same manufacturer.
model: GTS 250, GTS 300, GTV 250, GTV 300, LX 150, LXV 150, S 150, 946, BV 250 Tourer, BV 300 Tourer, BV 500, X9 500, MP3 250, MP3 500, Fly 50, LX50, S50, Primavera 50, Primavera 150, GTV 310
fix_procedure: 1. Check a machine by its own frame number against the current regulator record rather than against any summary, including this one. 2. Treat the 2006-2007 LX150 window as unverified: the index flags it and no campaign can be retrieved for it. 3. Do not read a missing record as proof that no campaign exists. 4. When querying the regulator's interface, treat a refused request as a failure and not as an empty result: a client that reads a refusal as 'no recalls' returns a confident and largely empty answer.

title: The CVT wear limits Piaggio publishes for its scooters — and the manual that gives one torque two different values
description: Piaggio publishes service limits for the belt-and-variator driveline, which this knowledge base has not carried before. The Beverly 125 service station manual (664602 IT, 664603 EN, 2007) gives the drive belt a minimum width of 21.5 mm against a standard of 22.5 plus or minus 0.2 mm, and a condition that does not depend on measurement at all: 'The rim bottom of the tooth must not have incisions or cracking; if it does, change the belt.' It also gives the driven half-pulley a standard diameter of 40.985 mm and a minimum of 40.96 mm. The Fly 125-150 4T workshop manual (633225) prints, for the variator rollers, a minimum permitted diameter of 18.5 mm and a standard diameter of 26 plus or minus 0.1 mm, together with a roller-container bushing maximum of 26.121 mm and a sliding-pulley bush minimum of 25.950 mm. Those two roller figures are quoted as printed. The same Beverly 125 manual states one torque twice and differently: its locking-torques table gives the clutch unit nut on the driven pulley as 45 to 50 Nm, and its refitting procedure, a few pages later and after the note that the nut is slightly asymmetric by design, gives 55 to 60 Nm. Both appear in the same 278-page document. The driveline is not the same across the range: Piaggio describes the smaller machines as having an automatic expandable pulley variator, torque server, V-belt and a dry self-ventilating centrifugal clutch, while the BV 350 has its centrifugal clutch running in an oil bath. No belt wear limit is published for the BV 350, whose manual says only to replace the belt as the scheduled maintenance table indicates, so the 21.5 mm figure must not be carried across to it. Generic CVT diagnosis is not this entry's subject; these are the figures Piaggio publishes for these machines.
causes: Carrying a wear limit across models that do not publish one
Taking a torque from the summary table without reading the procedure
fix_procedure: 1. Measure belt width against the model's own manual: 21.5 mm minimum is the Beverly 125 and Fly 125-150 figure, and the BV 350 publishes none. 2. Reject a belt with cracking or incisions at the tooth root whatever it measures. 3. On the Beverly 125's driven-pulley clutch nut, note that the manual gives both 45 to 50 Nm and 55 to 60 Nm; reconcile against the procedure you are following and record which you used. 4. Establish whether the clutch is dry or runs in oil before quoting a service method.

title: Engine family names as Piaggio writes them — i-Get, hpe and Hi-PER2 — and two names its manuals do not use
description: Piaggio's own documents name three families. The four-stroke injection engines are written 'Piaggio i-Get', hyphenated, in the owner's manuals: the Vespa Primavera S and Sprint S 125-150 manual (Ed. 01_05/2018, Cod. 1Q000662) gives 'Engine Single-cylinder, 4-stroke Piaggio i-Get' for both a 124 cm3 and a 155 cm3 engine sharing a stroke of 58.6 mm, three valves, a single overhead camshaft and electronic injection. The Medley manual (Ed. 02_01/2021, Cod. 1Q000842) gives the same family liquid-cooled with four valves and a start-and-stop system. 'hpe', expanded once by Piaggio as High Performance Engine, is the later family on the Beverly 300 and 400 and on the GTS 300 and 310. The two-stroke 50 is named separately: the Typhoon 50 service station manual (633665 to 633672, 2008) gives 'Engine type Two-stroke, single cylinder Piaggio Hi-PER2'. The Fly 125-150 workshop manual names a fourth, 'Piaggio LEADER'. Two names commonly attached to these machines do not appear in the manuals checked: across the Beverly 125, Fly 125-150, Typhoon 50 and MP3 400 service and workshop manuals, Quasar does not occur at all, and Master occurs only as the immobiliser master key and as the brake master-cylinder, never as an engine family. That is a statement about those four documents, not about every Piaggio publication. No Piaggio document read for this entry maps engine families to model years, so the family a given machine carries has to be read from its own specification table.
model: Primavera 125, Primavera 150, Sprint 125, Sprint 150, Medley 125, Medley 150, Liberty 125, Liberty 50, Beverly 300, Beverly 400, GTS 300, GTS 310, Typhoon 50, Fly 125, Fly 150
symptoms: what engine is in my vespa
causes: Using an enthusiast or press name that the service literature does not carry
Assuming an engine family from the model year rather than the specification table
fix_procedure: 1. Read the family from the machine's own specification table; Piaggio publishes no family-to-model-year map. 2. Expect i-Get on the four-stroke injection engines, hpe on the later Beverly and GTS engines, and Hi-PER2 on the two-stroke 50. 3. Searching the manuals for Quasar returns nothing, and Master returns the immobiliser key and the brake master-cylinder. 4. Confirm the exact spelling against the document before quoting it: Piaggio writes i-Get hyphenated and hpe in lower case.
